physical_harm: Injuries or death caused, briefly: The victim, Parvati, was abducted and subjected to sexual intercourse by Natuji.
number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged and how many were finally upheld: The main offence was abduction and sexual intercourse under Sections 363 and 366 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of POCSO Act. The appellants were not finally upheld as offenders under the POCSO Act.
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the statement of the victim (PW4) and her mother (PW3) were recorded, but noted that the statement of the mother was hearsay and could not be relied upon for proceeding against the appellants. The Court also noted that the victim's statement did not allege complicity of the appellants in the offence.
witness_credibility: The Court assessed the credibility of the witnesses by noting that the mother's statement was hearsay and could not be relied upon, and the victim's statement did not allege complicity of the appellants.

legal_representation.accused: D. N. Ray, Dillip Kumar Nayak, Ms. Disha Ray, Mrs. Sumita Ray, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Hemantika Wahi, Ms. Jesal Wahi, Ms. Puja Singh, Ms. Vishakha Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered on 27.05.2015, charge sheet filed under Sections 363 and 366 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of POCSO Act, trial proceeded against accused

appeal_history.high_court: Allowed the application, set aside the order of the trial court
appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's judgment

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court erred in reversing the order of the POCSO Judge rejecting the application under Section 319 Cr.P.C., and that the appellants should be proceeded against based on the victim's statement and her mother's statement.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court did not consider the Constitution Bench judgment in Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab & Others and that there was no valid reason for exercising the power under Section 319 Cr.P.C. against the appellants.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the power under Section 319 Cr.P.C. is discretionary and extraordinary, and should be exercised sparingly, with a test more than prima facie case but short of satisfaction that the evidence would lead to conviction.
precedent_relied_upon: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab & Others (2014) 3 SCC 92
